newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina sees 1997 trade gap exceeding $2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina sees 1997 trade gap exceeding $2 bln.

text.p: Argentina's trade deficit for 1997 is likely to be more than $2.0 billion, compared to original official forecasts of $1.5 billion, said a senior Economy Ministry official Thursday.
"If we want investments to exist, we have to accept a deficit in the trade balance," said Carlos Rodriguez, chief advisor to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, at a news conference.

Argentina posted a $71 million foreign trade surplus in 1996 and a $839 million surplus the year before, but the government says imports of capital and manufactured goods as a a result of strong growth will produce trade deficits.
It has forecast import growth this year of 25 percent, with exports expected to increase 16.7 percent.
